react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics differential set is dominated by arachidonic acid cascade intermediates, producing an overwhelming cross-paradigm signal in eicosanoid biosynthesis. Five metabolites — arachidonate (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-HETE (C04742), 5-HETE (C04805), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) — collectively hit Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167, FDR 1.25×10⁻¹³, fold-enrichment 1,430) in RaMP multi-DB ORA, Arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590) in MetaboAnalystR PSEA (score 1.0, rank 1), and the m/z-direct Mummichog Arachidonic acid metabolism network (p=0.0032, rank 1) plus Leukotriene metabolism (p=0.046, rank 4). The 5/5 pathway overlap across paradigms identifies this as the primary biological perturbation. Histamine (C00388) independently enriches KEGG:hsa00340 (Histidine metabolism, p=0.068) via Mummichog and MetaboAnalystR. Gentisic acid (C00628) maps to KEGG:hsa00350 (Tyrosine metabolism, p=0.171) in MetaboAnalystR, consistent with salicylate NSAID drug-action clusters seen in the SMPDB drug-pathway ORA results. Copper (C00070) and hypochlorite (C19697) are catalytic cofactors/co-oxidants for lipoxygenases but do not independently drive pathway enrichment. Dihydrothymine (C00906) represents a pyrimidine-degradation signal below enrichment thresholds. The convergent 5-lipoxygenase and 15-lipoxygenase arm activation, alongside COX-derived 15d-PGJ2 elevation, is consistent with a physiological or pharmacological intervention targeting the arachidonate flux node — most plausibly a selective 5-LOX inhibitor washout, inflammatory activation, or NSAID exposure pattern perturbing the balance between pro-inflammatory leukotriene and anti-inflammatory lipoxin/15-HETE branches.

Five metabolites — arachidonate (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-HETE (C04742), 5-HETE (C04805), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) — collectively hit Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167, FDR 1.25×10⁻¹³, fold-enrichment 1,430) in RaMP multi-DB ORA, Arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590) in MetaboAnalystR PSEA (score 1.0, rank 1), and the m/z-direct Mummichog Arachidonic acid metabolism network (p=0.0032, rank 1) plus Leukotriene metabolism (p=0.046, rank 4). The 5/5 pathway overlap across paradigms identifies this as the primary biological perturbation. Histamine (C00388) independently enriches KEGG:hsa00340 (Histidine metabolism, p=0.068) via Mummichog and MetaboAnalystR. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics differential set is dominated by arachidonic acid cascade intermediates, producing an overwhelming cross-paradigm signal in eicosanoid biosynthesis. Five metabolites — arachidonate (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-HETE (C04742), 5-HETE (C04805), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717) — collectively hit Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167, FDR 1.25×10⁻¹³, fold-enrichment 1,430) in RaMP multi-DB ORA, Arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590) in MetaboAnalystR PSEA (score 1.0, rank 1), and the m/z-direct Mummichog Arachidonic acid metabolism network (p=0.0032, rank 1) plus Leukotriene metabolism (p=0.046, rank 4). The 5/5 pathway overlap across paradigms identifies this as the primary biological perturbation. Histamine (C00388) independently enriches KEGG:hsa00340 (Histidine metabolism, p=0.068) via Mummichog and MetaboAnalystR. Gentisic acid (C00628) maps to KEGG:hsa00350 (Tyrosine metabolism, p=0.171) in MetaboAnalystR, consistent with salicylate NSAID drug-action clusters seen in the SMPDB drug-pathway ORA results. Copper (C00070) and hypochlorite (C19697) are catalytic cofactors/co-oxidants for lipoxygenases but do not independently drive pathway enrichment. Dihydrothymine (C00906) represents a pyrimidine-degradation signal below enrichment thresholds. The convergent 5-lipoxygenase and 15-lipoxygenase arm activation, alongside COX-derived 15d-PGJ2 elevation, is consistent with a physiological or pharmacological intervention targeting the arachidonate flux node — most plausibly a selective 5-LOX inhibitor washout, inflammatory activation, or NSAID exposure pattern perturbing the balance between pro-inflammatory leukotriene and anti-inflammatory lipoxin/15-HETE branches.
